models_evaluated: Third Opinion Mammograms (U-Net++ / Mask2Former, versions 1.0.0 and six updates)

links.outcome: Calibration tests against predefined AUC/accuracy thresholds before CMI implementation
links.effect: First two calibration tests failed thresholds (CalT1 accuracy 0.77; CalT2 AUC 0.78, accuracy 0.74), triggering developer updates; third test passed (AUC 0.84, accuracy 0.81) before implementation.
links.quote: The first two calibration tests failed to meet the predefined performance thresholds (0.80).

links.outcome: Repeat calibration testing after architectural model updates
links.effect: Repeat testing after updates detected regression: CalT6 accuracy 0.81 vs declared 0.92 (−11.96%), sensitivity −10.99%; subsequent CalT7 reached AUC 0.92, accuracy 0.90.
links.quote: Architectural updates (1st, 2nd, 5th, 6th) underwent repeat calibration testing ( Figure 4 , Tables 3,4 ).

links.outcome: Local performance vs developer-declared metrics
links.effect: CalT1 specificity 0.70 vs declared 0.88 (−20.45%); accuracy 0.77 vs 0.85 (−9.41%); CalT2 accuracy −12.94%.
links.quote: Subsequent calibration tests revealed initially subthreshold performance (AUC 0.83, accuracy 0.77, sensitivity 0.84, specificity 0.70), consistent with similar studies where early AI assessments uncover refinement needs ( 52 , 53 ).

links.outcome: Automatically logged technical defect (analysis failure) rates during prospective monitoring
links.effect: Technical defects exceeded 10% in 1 of 25 months (11.10%); average defect rate decreased from 3.0% to 0.8%.
links.quote: Technical defect rates exceeded 10% in only 1 of 25 months (group B defects: 11.10%; Figure 3A ).

unlisted_practices: Structured reporting of identified AI errors to developers prompting corrective updates within an iterative lifecycle testing framework

openai.sample_unit: mammograms in the prospective technical monitoring cohort
models_evaluated: Third Opinion Mammograms® (initial version 1.0.0 and subsequent updates; U-Net++ and Mask2Former architectures)

links.outcome: Detection of incomplete mammogram processing during predeployment functional testing
links.effect: Functional testing identified incomplete processing in one out of four mammography studies, prompting developer refinement.
links.quote: Functional testing identified one critical noncompliance: one out of four mammography studies was processed incompletely.

links.outcome: Local diagnostic performance relative to developer claims and acceptance thresholds
links.effect: Initial accuracy was 0.77 (0.69–0.85) versus declared 0.85; specificity was 0.70 (0.57–0.83) versus declared 0.88. The first two calibration tests failed the predefined 0.80 threshold.
links.quote: Subsequent calibration tests revealed initially subthreshold performance (AUC 0.83, accuracy 0.77, sensitivity 0.84, specificity 0.70), consistent with similar studies where early AI assessments uncover refinement needs ( 52 , 53 ).

links.outcome: Diagnostic performance following iterative error feedback, corrective updates, and repeat validation
links.effect: Across iterative testing, monitoring, and updates, AUC increased by 10.8% (from 0.83 to 0.92) and accuracy by 16.9% (from 0.77 to 0.90). Individual update effects could not be isolated.
links.quote: Over this time, AUC increased by 10.8% (from 0.83 to 0.92), accuracy by 16.9% (from 0.77 to 0.90), sensitivity by 4.8% (from 0.84 to 0.88), and specificity by 30.0% (from 0.70 to 0.91).

links.outcome: meeting predefined local performance thresholds
links.effect: Evaluation on historical data against a 0.80 performance threshold prevented the clinical deployment of the algorithm during the first two tests until updates allowed the third test to successfully satisfy the criteria.
links.quote: The first two calibration tests failed to meet the predefined performance thresholds (0.80).

links.outcome: performance validation after model updates
links.effect: The implementation protocol correctly required all architectural updates to undergo repeat calibration testing, ensuring that modifications were validated for diagnostic performance before monitoring continued.
links.quote: Architectural updates required repeat calibration testing for validation; non-architectural updates proceeded with routine testing or monitoring.

links.outcome: approval for clinical implementation
links.effect: Clinical deployment in the regional insurance program was strictly gated by a formal decision requiring the AI system to first meet predefined acceptance criteria for diagnostic accuracy and technical robustness.
links.quote: Implementation into routine clinical healthcare within the CMI program was permitted only after the system met predefined acceptance criteria for safe and effective deployment.

links.outcome: detection of functional integration errors
links.effect: Initial functional testing of the system successfully detected a critical data processing noncompliance where images were incompletely processed, which was subsequently resolved by the developers.
links.quote: Functional testing identified one critical noncompliance: one out of four mammography studies was processed incompletely.

links.outcome: technical error rates during monitoring
links.effect: Continuous technical and clinical monitoring over a 24-month period effectively tracked the system's operational stability, confirming that technical error rates exceeded the 10% threshold in only one observation period.
links.quote: The 24-month technical and clinical monitoring demonstrated stable AI system performance, with technical error rates remaining below threshold (<10%) in nearly all observation periods.

screen.practice: lifecycle testing with prospective monitoring and calibration across updates
screen.reason: The study evaluates a lifecycle-based monitoring and continuous quality-control framework during the real-world deployment of a mammography AI tool across 206 medical centers, measuring its effect on technical defects, clinical scores, and performance over time.

primary.practice: lifecycle-based testing, prospective monitoring, and continuous quality control
